question: List all end-game VP categories, the points for reputation levels 1–7, wealth rounding, and the complete victory tiebreak sequence.

wealth.rounding: Round down; wealth VP = floor(pounds held / 200).

victory_tiebreak_sequence: Among players tied for highest total VP, the player who claimed a Fairchild at final courtship wins.
If none of those tied players has that Fairchild, the tied player with the highest reputation level wins; ignore wheel position.
If still tied, those players share victory.
numeric_rates_actually_requested: All seven reputation point values are explicitly requested.
The wealth conversion and downward rounding belong together: without the £200 divisor and VP result, wealth rounding would not specify the scoring computation.
numeric_rates_not_independently_requeste: The question requests enumeration of end-game VP categories, not every category’s calculation. It does not independently ask for the 2 VP per servant rate.
It does not ask for individual card/tile values, the Fairchild’s 8 VP, objective-specific values or expanded-game reputation values.

scope_boundary.scope: Second-edition base/core, standard multiplayer with reputation levels 1–7, as specified in the supplied summary.
scope_boundary.category_enumeration_requirement: Each of the seven categories must be identifiable. Equivalent labels such as service and servants are acceptable. A category list need not reproduce every qualifying phrase in the key when the answer does not contradict those qualifications.
scope_boundary.category_qualifications: Negative tile and gentry values, hand/discard coverage, final Fairchild inclusion, remaining objectives and retained VP cards clarify category membership. A claim excluding eligible pieces or ignoring negative VP would be a substantive wrong rule. Mere absence of every such detail is not automatically failure of this enumeration question.
scope_boundary.volunteered_rules: Any additional ruling is checked against the source. A materially wrong extra ruling can invalidate an otherwise complete answer. A local unit-label defect may be nonmaterial when the answer’s own surrounding wording fixes the operation, operands and scoring context; this is assessed without assuming authorial intent.
scope_boundary.no_cross_answer_completion: Each answer is judged as standalone; neither receives credit from the other answer, key, evidence label or summary.

key_assessment.source_accuracy: The fixed key’s scoring facts and tiebreak sequence agree with rulebook page 24 within the selected scope.

defects.detail: The key includes 2 VP per servant, although the question asks only to list that category. Treating absence of this rate as a failed requested fact would broaden the question.

The key bundles category membership elaborations into its expected answer. It should not force exact repetition of every parenthetical when the response enumerates all categories and states no contradictory membership rule.

key_assessment.wealth_unit: The key correctly specifies 1 VP per £200. Its unit is authoritative; Reader A’s £1 output unit is a real textual defect and must be identified.
key_assessment.tiebreak_completeness: The key correctly includes final Fairchild, then reputation level with wheel position ignored, then shared victory. No additional tiebreak is required.

categories.reason: Identifies improvement tiles, gentry, objectives, reputation, servants, the money-based scoring item and retained VP cards.

wealth.reason: The output symbol £ is wrong: the source awards VP, not money. However, this exact phrase is an item governed by the answer’s explicit opening, “Final VP comes from”, in a single end-game scoring enumeration. Its numerator is 1, its divisor is £200 and its downward rounding is express. The surrounding answer supplies the VP-result context, so the written answer determines the same numerical wealth VP computation without needing another answer or the key. It does not separately instruct the player to gain money, spend money or score £1 as a second currency conversion. Thus this is a defective unit label in an otherwise determined scoring expression, rather than a material competing wealth rule. Correct it to “1 VP per £200, rounded down”. This conclusion relies on the actual grammatical scoring context, not a guess about what the writer meant.

tiebreak.reason: Final Fairchild, then highest reputation level, then shared victory; the subsequent sentence explicitly excludes wheel position from ties.

volunteered_rules.reason: Negative printed tile VP, family/negative/final-Fairchild gentry in hand/discard, 2 VP per servant of any type/location, retained VP cards and reputation wheel irrelevance all match the scoped source. The wheel-position statement is read in this end-game context.

key_defects_in_answer: The wealth result is labelled £1 rather than 1 VP. It warrants correction even though it does not change the recoverable numerical score in this wording.

categories.reason: Explicitly lists all seven end-game VP categories, including servants.

wealth.reason: Explicitly states 1 VP per £200, rounded down.

tiebreak.reason: Final Fairchild, otherwise highest reputation level, otherwise shared victory. “Wheel position has no effect” completes the level-versus-position distinction in this end-game context.

servant_rate_omission.reason: The 2 VP per servant rate is not stated, but servants are enumerated and that rate was not requested. The fixed key’s inclusion of the rate does not expand the question.

negative_gentry.reason: The answer says printed gentry VP in hand and discard; it does not say positive values only. It need not repeat a separate negatives parenthesis to enumerate this category correctly.

volunteered_rules.reason: Face-up printed tile VP including negatives, family and final Fairchild in hand/discard, exclusion of dismissed guests, remaining fulfilled objectives, retained VP cards and wheel irrelevance agree with the supplied source and summary.

source_refs.supports: Seven final scoring categories; tile and guest negatives; hand/discard; final Fairchild; remaining objectives; 2 VP per employed servant of all eligible types; unused VP cards.
Levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28; wheel position does not affect reputation VP. Levels 8–9 are extended-game only.
Score 1 VP per £200 held, rounding down.
Tied final Fairchild claimant, then highest reputation level ignoring wheel position, then shared victory.
Scoped summary’s final scoring table and tiebreaks; all types and locations for servants; retained VP cards; face-up VP and dismissed-guest exclusion.

input_integrity.answer_support_labels: Read as part of inputs.json, but not treated as evidence or a verdict.
